300.author: wyhohyw
300.body:
﻿Daily CI gave RACE and FACT one shared 10-minute deadline. RACE finished, then the judge was killed while citation checking was still running, so citation accuracy and verification coverage were never recorded. On the 13 and 14 October nightlies every DRB case showed this. Forty minutes covers those runs except a DRB-64 report that cites the same manuals as dozens of distinct statements; thirty minutes still clips that report and leaves only about three minutes of margin on the next-slowest cases.

## Evaluation deadline
`.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` sets `E2E_DRB_EVAL_TIMEOUT_MS` to `2400000`. The local default stays one hour. The DeepResearchBench README's daily evaluation budget matches this deadline. Research shard jobs remain capped at 240 minutes, so the longer judge fits inside the job.

## Validation
`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. This commit changes a nightly workflow constant and its README; those layers do not execute the real DRB judge. WSL on this machine has bubblewrap, but the fresh worktree has no `node_modules`, and installing it would not observe the 40-minute deadline. The check is the next nightly after this merges and syncs to GitHub: each DRB case should record citation accuracy and verification coverage instead of `running`.

## E2E user journeys
Not applicable. No UI, API, CLI, or session behavior changes. Delivery assertions are unchanged; only the separate judge deadline in daily CI is longer.
300.head: codex/drb-eval-40m
300.title: ci: allow DRB citation scoring forty minutes

302.author: wyhohyw
302.body:
Re-running a job left the previous attempt's artifact in place. Coverage then downloaded that older package by name and failed a passed UT, because the manifest still said the first attempt failed. Closes #301.

## What changes

`actions/upload-artifact@v4` keeps an existing artifact unless `overwrite` is true. On PR #295, run 38526631198, the failed UT uploaded `ut-coverage` (`status: FAIL`, 3821/3822). The re-run passed and uploaded a second package with the same name. Coverage ran with `needs.ut.result=success` and read the 07:30 package, so `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` reported incomplete coverage.

Uploads that a later job downloads by exact name now replace the previous attempt:

- `ut-coverage`
- `st-coverage`
- `mocked-e2e-plan`
- `real-e2e-plan`

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` fails if a workflow downloads an artifact by exact name and the matching upload omits `overwrite: true`.

## Validation

- WSL, `node --test --test-name-pattern "latest attempt" .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: 1 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. This change is GitHub Actions artifact metadata. Those layers do not observe the artifact store, and the contract test is what locks the flag.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. No product UI, API, CLI, or run path changes. The bug is which artifact a later GitHub Actions job downloads after a job re-run.
302.head: fix/ci-coverage-artifact-rerun
302.title: fix(ci): replace artifacts from a previous job attempt
